quizzes.title: Kavach and the North-East Tunnel
quizzes.passage: Transport and connectivity is one of the topics covered in the February 2026 current affairs section of the booklet. The first item is Kavach, which the booklet describes as India's Indigenous Automated Train Protection System. Kavach has been deployed across more than 2200 route kilometres in India, and it is presented as a rail safety system. The second item is a road-cum-rail project. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved an underwater twin tube road-cum-rail tunnel, with the stated aim of boosting connectivity in the North-East. The booklet places the tunnel in Assam and states that the total length of the project is 33.7 km. The Kavach entry is listed first, and the tunnel entry follows it on the same page. The section lists the figures for each item, along with the name of the organisation behind the system. Both items are part of the same chapter heading, so a reader can see how a safety system and an infrastructure project are grouped under one topic. The tunnel is described as a twin tube structure, and the booklet links the project to the North-East region. The booklet presents both items as part of its February 2026 coverage of transport. Each item is given a short entry with its key features.

questions.q: Kavach was developed by which organisation?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Kavach was developed by the Research Designs & Standards Organisation of Indian Railways.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an objective of Kavach?
options: Enhancing situational awareness for loco pilots
questions.explanation: The booklet lists collision prevention, avoiding signal passing at danger and situational awareness for loco pilots as objectives.

questions.q: How long is the underwater twin tube portion of the tunnel?
questions.explanation: The underwater twin tube tunnel is 15.79 km within a total project length of 33.7 km.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The underwater twin tube tunnel lies beneath the Brahmaputra River.
Reason (R): The underwater section of the tunnel is the full 33.7 km length of the project.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The tunnel is under the Brahmaputra, but its underwater section is 15.79 km, not the full 33.7 km.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Kavach   ->   A. NH-15
II. Gohpur   ->   B. RDSO
III. Numaligarh   ->   C. 15.79 km
IV. Underwater twin tube tunnel   ->   D. NH-715
questions.explanation: Kavach is developed by RDSO, Gohpur is on NH-15, Numaligarh is on NH-715 and the underwater tube is 15.79 km.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Kavach is designed to enhance situational awareness for loco pilots.
II. Kavach was developed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
III. The underwater twin tube tunnel is 33.7 km long.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since Kavach was developed by RDSO and the underwater tube is 15.79 km.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Kavach is designed to prevent train collisions.
The tunnel links Gohpur with Numaligarh under the Brahmaputra.
The underwater twin tube tunnel measures 33.7 km.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Two statements are correct, and the underwater tube is 15.79 km rather than 33.7 km.

quizzes.title: Kavach and Tunnel Figures
quizzes.passage: Transport and connectivity is covered in the February 2026 current affairs section of the booklet, which places it among the topics for the month. The section begins with Kavach, described as India's Indigenous Automated Train Protection System. The booklet presents Kavach as a rail safety system and gives its deployment in India in route kilometres. The section then covers a major tunnel project. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved an underwater twin tube road-cum-rail tunnel, with the stated purpose of boosting connectivity in the North-East. The tunnel is described as a road-cum-rail link that passes under a river in Assam. It is linked to two national highways at its two ends, which the booklet names by their numbers. The booklet gives figures for the whole project and for the underwater part of the tunnel, and it names the organisation that developed Kavach. Each entry is short and lists its key features in a few lines. Both items appear on the same page, with the Kavach entry first and the tunnel entry next. Kavach is listed first in the section, and the booklet gives its objectives in a short list. The section thus shows a rail safety system and a road-rail infrastructure project placed side by side under one topic, with the figures and names given in the booklet's own entries.

questions.q: Kavach has been deployed across how many route kilometres in India? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Kavach is deployed across over 2200 route kilometres in India.

questions.q: What is the total length of the tunnel project, in km? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the total tunnel project length as 33.7 km.

questions.q: What is the length, in km, of the underwater twin tube tunnel? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the underwater twin tube tunnel is 15.79 km long.

questions.q: Which organisation developed Kavach? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Kavach was developed by the Research Designs & Standards Organisation, abbreviated RDSO.

questions.q: Numaligarh is on which national highway? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the tunnel connects Gohpur on NH-15 with Numaligarh on NH-715.

questions.q: Under which river does the underwater tunnel pass? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the underwater tunnel under the Brahmaputra River in Assam.

questions.q: Gohpur is on which national highway? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the tunnel connects Gohpur on NH-15 with Numaligarh on NH-715.

quizzes.title: Mercury, Summits and Cyber Initiatives
quizzes.passage: Space and cyber security is one of the topic areas in the February 2026 section of the booklet. The space item concerns Mercury, which the booklet describes as the planet closest to the Sun. The booklet reports that data from a spacecraft revealed numerous bright streaks scattered across the planet's surface. A separate part of the entry lists further facts about Mercury, including several key discoveries made about the planet. The booklet lists these facts in short bullet-style lines, with one fact on each line. The cyber items form the second part of the section. The booklet describes the Global CyberPeace Summit 2026 as an event that concluded. The summit is listed alongside other entries in the cyber section. The summit entry is followed by a programme and two bodies, in the order given. Another entry is a programme that builds talent in cyber and AI, and the booklet notes that it was launched in partnership with another organisation. The booklet also introduces two bodies in this area, one working on future risks and one working in the automotive field. Each of these items is listed with its own name and a short description in the booklet. Each entry is brief, and the section keeps the space and cyber items under one heading, in that order.

questions.q: Data from which NASA mission revealed numerous bright streaks across Mercury's surface?
questions.explanation: The booklet credits NASA's MESSENGER mission with revealing the bright streaks on Mercury's surface.

questions.q: Mercury's large core is described in the booklet as being rich in which element?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Mercury has a large, iron-rich core.

questions.q: Water ice was confirmed on Mercury in which type of craters?
questions.explanation: The booklet says water ice was confirmed in permanently shadowed polar craters.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Mercury has no moons or rings.
Reason (R): Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but Mercury's small size does not explain the absence of moons or rings.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Global CyberPeace Summit 2026   ->   A. Quantum computing risks
II. AI Scholarship Programme   ->   B. New Delhi
III. Global Quantum Threat Alliance   ->   C. Connected, autonomous and electric vehicles
IV. CoE on Automotive Cybersecurity   ->   D. EC Council partnership
questions.explanation: The summit concluded in New Delhi, the AI programme has an EC Council partnership, the alliance addresses quantum computing risks and the CoE covers connected, autonomous and electric vehicles.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Mercury is the fastest orbiting planet around the Sun.
II. The Global CyberPeace Summit 2026 concluded in Mumbai.
III. The Global CyberPeace Summit 2026 was organised by NASA.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the summit concluded in New Delhi and was organised by CyberPeace.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Mercury has moons.
The Global Quantum Threat Alliance addresses future cyber risks arising from quantum computing.
Mercury is the densest planet after Earth.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Two statements are correct, because Mercury has no moons and the other two statements match the booklet.

quizzes.title: Mercury Facts and Cyber Bodies
quizzes.passage: Space and cyber security is the other broad area covered in the February 2026 section of the booklet. The space entry is about Mercury. The booklet describes the planet as the closest to the Sun and the smallest in the Solar System, and it says it is the fastest orbiting planet around the Sun. Data from a NASA spacecraft is reported to have revealed numerous bright streaks across the planet's surface. The booklet also lists key discoveries, which include the presence of water ice in certain shaded areas and a large core. The space entry comes first, and the cyber entries follow it in the same section of the booklet. The Global CyberPeace Summit 2026 is described as an event that concluded, and it was organised by CyberPeace. Another entry describes a programme created to build global cyber and AI talent, which was launched in partnership with another body. A further entry describes an alliance that aims to address future cyber risks, and a centre of excellence that focuses on securing vehicles of several kinds. The booklet keeps the space and cyber items in separate parts of the section, and each part has short entries that list their main facts. Mercury is shown as the first entry in the space part of the section.

questions.q: How many natural satellites (moons) does Mercury have? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Mercury has no moons or rings.

questions.q: The AI Scholarship Programme was launched in partnership with which body? (name only)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the programme was launched in partnership with the EC Council.

questions.q: In which city was the Global CyberPeace Summit 2026 concluded? (city only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Global CyberPeace Summit 2026 concluded in New Delhi.

questions.q: Mercury's large core is described as what kind of rich? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Mercury as having a large, iron-rich core.

questions.q: The Global Quantum Threat Alliance addresses future cyber risks arising from which technology? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the alliance addresses future cyber risks arising from quantum computing.

questions.q: Water ice on Mercury was confirmed in permanently shadowed craters near which part of the planet? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says water ice was confirmed in permanently shadowed polar craters.

questions.q: Mercury is the densest planet after which planet? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Mercury is the second densest planet after Earth.

quizzes.title: Pharmacopoeia, APEDA and Rafah
quizzes.passage: The institutions and places part of the February 2026 booklet includes the following items. The first body is the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission. The booklet describes the Pharmacopoeia as a compendium that defines standards for the identity, purity, strength and quality of medicines. The Commission is shown as prescribing quality standards for drugs that are manufactured, sold and consumed in India. Its key publications include the Indian Pharmacopoeia, which is described as the official book of drug quality standards in India, and the National Formulary of India. The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission is presented first, and the APEDA entry follows it. The booklet gives the Commission's establishment and headquarters in its entry. The second body is APEDA, the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority. Its functions include facilitating and promoting the export of agricultural and processed food products, and it also has an inspection and quality control role. The third item is a place: the Rafah Crossing in Gaza. The booklet says the crossing allows limited movement and humanitarian access, and it lists the crossing among other border points in Gaza. The Rafah Crossing entry is the last item in the places section of the booklet. Each entry is short, and the booklet arranges them under separate headings for organisations and for places.

questions.q: In which year was APEDA established?
questions.explanation: The booklet says APEDA was established in 1986.

questions.q: APEDA's headquarters is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the APEDA headquarters in New Delhi.

questions.q: Under which ministry does the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission function?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare as the administrative ministry of the Commission.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Indian Pharmacopoeia is a legally binding compendium.
Reason (R): The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission was established in 2005.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but the year of establishment does not explain why the compendium is legally binding.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Formulary of India   ->   C. Headquartered in Ghaziabad
II. APEDA   ->   A. Often referred to as Gaza's Lifeline
III. Rafah Crossing   ->   D. Statutory body under the APEDA Act 1985
IV. Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission   ->   B. Promotes rational use of medicines
questions.explanation: The National Formulary promotes rational use of medicines, APEDA is a statutory body, Rafah is called Gaza's Lifeline and the Commission is headquartered in Ghaziabad.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. APEDA marked 40 years of promoting India's agricultural exports.
II. The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission signed five MoUs.
III. The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission is headquartered in New Delhi.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the Commission signed three MoUs and is headquartered in Ghaziabad.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The Rafah Crossing was partially reopened after two years.
APEDA was established in 1975.
The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission signed three MoUs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Two statements are correct, since APEDA was established in 1986 rather than 1975.

quizzes.title: Institutions and the Rafah Crossing
quizzes.passage: The February 2026 booklet includes an institutions section and a places section. The first body is the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, which the booklet says was established in 2005. The Pharmacopoeia is described as a legally binding compendium, and it defines standards for identity, purity, strength and quality of medicines. The Indian Pharmacopoeia is described as the official book of drug quality standards in India. The Commission prescribes quality standards for drugs manufactured, sold and consumed in India. Its key publications are the Indian Pharmacopoeia and the National Formulary of India. The second body is APEDA, which marked 40 years of promoting India's agricultural exports. APEDA promotes the export of agricultural and processed food products, and its inspection and quality control work covers meat products and processed foods. Its headquarters is in New Delhi, and its chairman is appointed by the Government of India. The Commission's publications are presented in the same entry as its functions. The places section covers the Rafah Crossing in Gaza, which was partially reopened after two years. The crossing allows limited movement and humanitarian access. The booklet lists the crossing among other border points in Gaza. Rafah is described in the booklet as a crossing, and the entry sits under the places heading. Each entry is short, and the entries are arranged under organisation and place headings.

questions.q: In which year was APEDA established? (year only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says APEDA was established in 1986.

questions.q: How many MoUs did the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission sign? (number only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Commission signed 3 MoUs to strengthen medicine safety, quality and pharmacovigilance.

questions.q: In which city is the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission headquartered? (city only)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the headquarters of the Commission as Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: APEDA acts as the secretariat of which board for certification of export-related bodies? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says APEDA acts as the secretariat to the National Accreditation Board.

questions.q: APEDA is a statutory body under which Act? (year of the Act only)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes APEDA as a statutory body under the APEDA Act 1985.

questions.q: Under which Union ministry does the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission function? (ministry name without the words Ministry of)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare as the administrative ministry of the Commission.

questions.q: The Rafah Crossing is often referred to as Gaza's what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Rafah Crossing is often referred to as Gaza's Lifeline.
